note: Foreign-born population figures come in two vintages. The accredited baseline is the 2021/22 Census (Census 2021 for England, Wales and Northern Ireland; Census 2022 for Scotland). In May 2026 ONS published a rolled-forward mid-2024 estimate of the non-UK-born population (13,115,000, about 18.9% of the population), an official statistic in development and provisional; ONS produced no June 2025 estimate because 2025 deaths data are not yet available, and it publishes no percentage. Citizenship and settlement figures come from Home Office Immigration system statistics (year ending December 2025).

metrics.metric_name: Foreign-born (non-UK born) population of the UK
metrics.source_name: Migration Observatory (University of Oxford), Migrants in the UK: An Overview, based on the 2021/22 Census
metrics.notes: The accredited 2021/22 Census figure. The foreign-born population has continued to rise since 2021; ONS's provisional rolled-forward estimate for mid-2024 is held separately as foreign-born-population-mid-2024.

metrics.metric_name: Foreign-born share of total UK population
metrics.source_name: Migration Observatory (University of Oxford), Migrants in the UK: An Overview
metrics.notes: Roughly one in six residents, of a total population of 66.9 million at the time. Up from about 9% in 2004. This is the accredited 2021/22 Census figure; for the later provisional estimate see foreign-born-share-mid-2024.

metrics.metric_name: Foreign-born (non-UK born) population of the UK, mid-2024 (provisional)
metrics.source_name: ONS, Long-term international migration, provisional: year ending December 2025 (Table 3)
metrics.notes: ONS rolled-forward estimate from a Census 2021 (England, Wales, Northern Ireland) and Census 2022 (Scotland) baseline. An official statistic in development and provisional, subject to revision. ONS gives no June 2025 estimate because 2025 deaths of people born outside the UK are not yet available. Of the total, 3,871,000 were EU+ born and 9,244,000 non-EU+ born. Do not confuse with the lower APS-based ad hoc estimate of about 10.6 million, which uses a different population base and does not reconcile with the mid-2024 UK total.

metrics.metric_name: Foreign-born share of total UK population, mid-2024 (calculated, provisional)
metrics.source_name: Calculated from ONS Long-term international migration (provisional, year ending December 2025) and the ONS mid-2024 UK population estimate
metrics.notes: Calculated by this project: 13,115,000 non-UK-born (ONS LTIM provisional, mid-2024) divided by the accredited mid-2024 UK population of 69,281,400 (ONS mid-year estimate, published 26 September 2025) is 18.93%, shown here as 18.9%. ONS does not publish this share directly. The numerator is an official statistic in development and provisional, so treat the share as approximate; it is often rounded to about 19%.

metrics.source_name: Migration Observatory (University of Oxford), Migrants in the UK: An Overview
metrics.notes: Foreign-citizen (non-British nationality) share, up from about 5% in 2004. Differs from the foreign-born group: many migrants naturalise, and some UK-born residents are non-citizens.

metrics.source_name: ONS, Population estimates for the UK: mid-2024 (released 26 September 2025)
metrics.notes: Latest official mid-year estimate (69.3 million). Up 755,300 (1.1%) on mid-2023, with net international migration of 738,700 the main driver. Accredited official statistics.

metrics.metric_name: Largest country of birth among foreign-born, India (share)
metrics.source_name: Migration Observatory (University of Oxford), Migrants in the UK: An Overview
metrics.notes: India was the largest single country of birth (9%). The top five, India (9%), Poland (8%), Pakistan (6%), Romania (5%), Ireland (4%), together accounted for 32% of the foreign-born population.

metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending March 2026, settlement and citizenship
metrics.notes: Down 12% on the year ending March 2025 (269,178). Naturalisation 165,429; registration 71,083. Applications rose 18% to 312,063 over the same period. Supersedes the year ending December 2025 figure of 235,782.

metrics.metric_name: Settlement (Indefinite Leave to Remain, excluding EU Settlement Scheme) grants
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending March 2026, settlement and citizenship
metrics.notes: Down 11% on the year ending March 2025 (170,237). Excludes EU Settlement Scheme settled status. Refugee settlement grants within this fell 53% to 19,960. Supersedes the year ending December 2025 figure of 146,405.

metrics.metric_name: EU Settlement Scheme settled status grants
metrics.source_name: Home Office, Immigration system statistics, year ending March 2026, settlement and citizenship
metrics.notes: About 4.5 million settled-status grants have been issued since the scheme launched in 2018. Classified as Official Statistics (not accredited). Includes an estimated 100,300 automated grants, from an estimated 103,820 automated in total. RECONCILED against table EUSS_QTR, whose settled conclusions for the four quarters to March 2026 sum to 270,235: the difference is the automated estimate, which no summary table carries. The published figure appears in the bulletin narrative only, which is why the evidence entry names no table.

metrics.metric_name: Share of foreign-born residents living in London and the South East
metrics.source_name: Migration Observatory (University of Oxford), Migrants in the UK: An Overview
metrics.notes: About 47% of foreign-born residents lived in London and the South East, against 27% of the overall population.

metrics.metric_name: Share of London residents born abroad
metrics.source_name: Migration Observatory (University of Oxford), Migrants in the UK: An Overview
metrics.notes: More than 40% of London residents were born abroad, the highest of any region. National average 16%. Lowest: North East (7%), Wales (7%), Northern Ireland (9%).
